root_cause.text: The macvlan_get_size() function failed to reserve netlink attribute space for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF, even though macvlan_fill_info() conditionally includes this 4-byte attribute when port->bc_cutoff != 1, causing buffer overflow when serializing interface attributes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `+ nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF */` to macvlan_get_size(), which was missing since the original commit 954d1fa1ac93 that introduced the nla_put_s32() call for this attribute in macvlan_fill_info(). The CVE description confirms that macvlan_fill_info() conditionally includes the attribute but macvlan_get_size() did not account for it, causing nla_put_s32() to fail with -EMSGSIZE when the netlink skb runs out of space.

intent_record.intent_summary: Account for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF attribute size in netlink message buffer calculation to prevent truncation or overflow.
intent_record.what: Added a single line to the macvlan_get_size() function that includes an additional nla_total_size(4) calculation for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF attribute in the netlink message size computation.
intent_record.how: This change increases the calculated netlink attribute buffer size by 4 bytes to account for a new IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF attribute. At runtime, when macvlan_get_size() is called to determine the required netlink message size, it will now return a larger value that includes space for this additional attribute, preventing potential buffer overflows or truncation when the attribute is subsequently added to the netlink response.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement represents the last attribute size calculation in macvlan_get_size() before the closing parenthesis. The vulnerable code is missing the nla_total_size(4) for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF attribute that should be added after this line. Since macvlan_fill_info() conditionally includes the IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF attribute (4 bytes) when port->bc_cutoff != 1, but macvlan_get_size() does not reserve space for it, this causes a buffer overflow when serializing interface attributes. The fix requires adding an additional nla_total_size(4) call for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF to properly account for the attribute space in the netlink message buffer calculation.

commit d4bff72c8401e6f56194ecf455db70ebc22929e2
Author: Thomas Karlsson <thomas.karlsson@paneda.se>
Date:   Wed Dec 2 19:49:58 2020 +0100

    macvlan: Support for high multicast packet rate
    
    Background:
    Broadcast and multicast packages are enqueued for later processing.
    This queue was previously hardcoded to 1000.
    
    This proved insufficient for handling very high packet rates.
    This resulted in packet drops for multicast.
    While at the same time unicast worked fine.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability root cause states that macvlan_get_size() failed to reserve netlink attribute space for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF (or BC_QUEUE_LEN attributes), causing buffer overflow. However, examining this commit diff, the macvlan_get_size() function at lines 1617-1620 DOES include the necessary space reservations: '+ nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_QUEUE_LEN */ + nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_QUEUE_LEN_USED */'. Additionally, macvlan_fill_info() at lines 1666-1668 properly adds these attributes with nla_put_u32() calls. This commit introduces both the attributes and their corresponding size calculations together, so the fix is already present in this commit. The vulnerable construct (missing size reservation) is not present in this code.
